headline: The U.S. Army will detonate degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, on Nov. 20 at approximately 12:00 PM CST. Lead azide is a highly sensitive primary explosive used in detonators. The stockpile is 68 barrels that have sat at the plant for nearly 20 years. The material has recrystallized, which makes it more sensitive to shock and friction, and the Army has deemed it unsafe to move. Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) teams will destroy it in place, in coordination with the EPA. Army modeling predicts the detonation will create a plume carrying lead particles, which will spread through the air and settle on surfaces downwind. The Army is publishing two exposure maps, one for airborne lead and one for surface dust. The current maps are posted below, but the Army says they may be updated right up until the detonation. About 55 nearby homes have been asked to temporarily relocate. Anyone who lives or works in the affected area is advised what precautions to take before, during and after the detonation.

headline: Retired U.S. Navy Admiral Philip Davidson, whose 2021 testimony gave rise to the “Davidson Window” for China achieving the required capability in order to invade Taiwan by 2027, said on a podcast released Friday that he hopes he was wrong, according to TWZ. “If I’m wrong, that means the things we recommended from Indo-Pacific Command...have been effective. A roughly $14 billion package, largely PAC-3 and NASAMS air defense missiles, cleared Congress’s informal review in January but has not received President Trump’s sign off and has been on hold since his summit with Chinese President Xi in May, according to the AP. Separately, Taiwan has a backlog of almost $30 billion in previously approved arms awaiting delivery, according to George Mason University’s Taiwan Security Monitor. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said in May that arms sales to Taiwan were paused to ensure the U.S. has the munitions it needs for Iran operations.
